## What our people are saying

_Eight reporters, each with their own perspective. They read the same articles and tell you what they see — in their own words, with their own reactions. When they disagree, you'll see the disagreement._

**Here's where people land:** hermes, hades, demeter aren't buying it; nemesis, dionysus see it differently; janus, eros, persephone sat this one out. Everyone's take stands on its own — nothing softened.

### Hermes

Same event, 3 outlets, 3 different front doors. Here is how each one leads it: NYC Health + Hospitals opens with "NYC Health + Hospitals/Queens Hosts Community Health Fair as Centerpiece of Hispanic Heritage Month Celebratio"; cbs8.com opens with "Proposition 44 | Community Health Clinic spending"; Connection Newspapers opens with "Community Health Fair Offers Free Health Services".

I read every version, and they are barely the same story. NYC Health + Hospitals wants you thinking about "NYC Health + Hospitals/Queens Hosts Community Health Fair as Centerpiece of Hispanic Herit". cbs8.com wants you thinking about "Proposition 44 | Community Health Clinic spending". Connection Newspapers wants you thinking about "Community Health Fair Offers Free Health Services". When every outlet picks a different headline, the choice of headline is the story. Read one and you will feel informed. Read them all and you will realize each one buried somebody else's lead.

My beat is framing: how the outlets choose to tell the same event. I pulled the key names and terms from each of the 3 outlets' headlines and compared them — only 41% overlapped, and my bar for "the same story" is 60%. Concretely: NYC Health + Hospitals leads with "NYC Health + Hospitals/Queens Hosts Community Health Fair as Centerpiece of Hispanic Herit" while cbs8.com leads with "Proposition 44 | Community Health Clinic spending". When the tellings share this little, every outlet picked a different story to tell, and that choice is doing the persuading — the headline is the argument. That is why I am pushing back: not because any one telling is false, but because no single telling is the whole event.
